1	# MPS3 (FePS3, MnPS3, NiPS3, CoPS3): expert Raman notes
2	
3	Numbers as printed in the cited source. "corpus p." = page of the group Lit-RAG PDF copy. Peak labels P1, P2, ...
4	are paper-specific (ordered by frequency within each paper), so the same label means different modes in different
5	papers: always map by frequency. Not used by design: the papers behind Zenodo 23300631 (NiPS3) and 20449397 (CoPS3).
6	
7	## Shared structure and irreps
8	- Bulk monoclinic C2h; Gamma = 8Ag + 7Bg + 6Au + 9Bu (NiPS3). Backscattering: Ag and Bg in XX, only Bg in XY. Monolayer
9	  is D3d (Kim et al. 2019, Nat. Commun. 10, 345, arXiv 1901.10890, corpus p.2).
10	- High-frequency modes (above about 200 cm-1) are internal (P2S6)4- vibrations common to the family; low-frequency
11	  modes involve the metal ion and are the magnetically sensitive ones (Kim 2019, corpus p.2; Vaclavkova et al. 2021,
12	  PRB 104, 134437, arXiv 2108.10945, corpus p.2).
13	- Magnetic types (consensus framing): FePS3 Ising, NiPS3 XXZ (XY-like), MnPS3 Heisenberg (Lim et al. 2021, Curr.
14	  Appl. Phys. 21, 1, doi:10.1016/j.cap.2020.09.017, corpus p.3).
15	- Three mechanisms for magnetic signatures: zone folding by the AFM supercell, spin-phonon / spin-spin interactions,
16	  and interference of phonons with electronic transitions (Fano) (Oliva et al. 2023, PRB 107, 104415,
17	  doi:10.1103/physrevb.107.104415, corpus p.2). In MnPS3 the magnetic and chemical cells coincide, so no zone folding.
18	
19	## FePS3 (T_N about 118 to 120 K)
20	- Above T_N a broad low-frequency band (about 105 cm-1, "P0") plus four modes 150 to 400 cm-1; below T_N it resolves
21	  into sharp zone-folded peaks P1 to P3 and P4 gains intensity; a magnon-gap mode M appears (Ghosh et al. 2021, PRB
22	  103, 064431, doi:10.1103/physrevb.103.064431, corpus p.1-2; Vaclavkova 2021, corpus p.2, Fig. 1a).
23	- Magnon at 121 cm-1 (about 15 meV, matches neutron data), blueshifting on cooling (Liu et al. 2021, PRL 127, 097401,
24	  doi:10.1103/physrevlett.127.097401, corpus p.2; 4L). In few layers it was seen only well below T_N (about 60 K)
25	  near 120 cm-1 (Ghosh 2021, corpus p.1).
26	- Field along c: M splits into branches; the lower branch anticrosses P1 to P3 (magnon-polarons), and an extra R1 mode
27	  appears at high field (Vaclavkova 2021, corpus p.3, Fig. 1b; Liu 2021, up to 30 T).
28	- Thickness: DISPUTED. Lee et al. 2016 (Nano Lett. 16, 7433, arXiv 1608.04169) report Ising order to 1L with little
29	  T_N change; Wang et al. 2016 (2D Mater. 3, 031009) report a T_N drop with thinning (both relayed by Martin-Perez
30	  et al. 2023, ACS Nano, doi:10.1021/acsnano.2c11654, corpus p.2). Magnetometry on 5 to 9 layer flakes gives T_N
31	  about 4 K below bulk (114.3 versus 118 K) (Martin-Perez 2023, corpus p.5). Strain alone can lower T_N (same, p.2).
32	- Air: 2L FePS3 Raman stable up to 6 days in ambient (Lee 2016, Suppl. Fig. S16, corpus p.38).
33	
34	## MnPS3 (T_N about 78 K)
35	- Mode near 155 cm-1 involves Mn; it disappears near 80 K and a mode at 151 cm-1 appears below about 50 K (130L flake,
36	  488 nm, 0.17 mW to avoid heating) (Sun et al. 2019, J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 10, 3087, doi:10.1021/acs.jpclett.9b00758,
37	  corpus p.2, p.4-5). Sun et al. also infer transitions near 120, 80 and 55 K (corpus p.2).
38	- T_N from broadening, abrupt redshift and spectral-weight gain of the 155 cm-1 peak: about 78 K bulk, about 66 K 3L
39	  (Lim 2021, corpus p.2, p.11).
40	- Frequencies are nearly constant from 2L to bulk (weak interlayer coupling); 3L-4L show only P5, P6; 2L only P6; 1L
41	  gave no signal (degradation or weak scattering) (Sun 2019, corpus p.3-4).
42	- Below T_N (Oliva 2023, 3.4 K): a mode near 117 cm-1 vanishes and new peaks appear near 194, 370, 565, 605 cm-1, of
43	  unknown origin; the mode near 154 cm-1 is the most T-sensitive. Its two-magnon interpretation is ruled out
44	  (two-magnon expected near 177 cm-1); origin DISPUTED (Oliva 2023, corpus p.4, p.7-8).
45	- A spin-glass-like short-range regime below about 120 K is proposed from linewidths (Oliva 2023, corpus p.6).
46	
47	## NiPS3 (bulk T_N 155 K)
48	- P2 (near 180 cm-1) splits into Ag (XX, higher) and Bg (XY, lower) below T_N; Delta P2 tracks the susceptibility and
49	  is near zero at 295 K (Kim 2019, corpus p.4-5, Fig. 4). Two-magnon continuum in XY grows and blueshifts on cooling;
50	  the Fano asymmetry |1/q| of a high-frequency phonon (P9) rises below T_N (Kim 2019, corpus p.3-5, Fig. 3).
51	- Thickness: order persists to 2L with slightly lower T_N; Kim 2019 conclude it is suppressed in 1L (same on hBN and
52	  SiO2). DISPUTED: Kim T. Y. et al. 2021 (Nano Lett. 21, 10114, doi:10.1021/acs.nanolett.1c03992, corpus p.2, p.5)
53	  argue 1L orders but the D3d monolayer's three zigzag domains make Delta P2 unmeasurable in XX/XY. Discala et al.
54	  2024 (Adv. Phys. Res. 3, 2300096) also question bulk-Hamiltonian assumptions (corpus p.1-2).
55	- Multiphonon peaks near 210, 590, 800 cm-1 are resonance dependent and not magnetic (Kim 2019, corpus p.4).
56	
57	## CoPS3
58	- Monolayer about 0.80 nm. P2 near 149 cm-1 splits into P2' (Ag) and P2'' (Bg) at low T (XY vs XX); Delta P2 > 8 cm-1
59	  below about 56 K, near zero above about 100 K; bulk transition 118 K (Liu Q. et al. 2021, PRB 103, 235411,
60	  doi:10.1103/physrevb.103.235411, corpus p.3-4, Figs. 2-3). Splitting is layer independent (intralayer distortion).
61	- Two-magnon bands near 350 and 600 cm-1 in XY in 1L; Fano P8 below 56 K (Liu 2021, corpus p.4-5, Fig. 4). The
62	  authors interpret few-layer behaviour as BKT-like (T_KT about 100 K); interpretation, not consensus.
63	
64	## Polarization, excitation, quality
65	- Use XX and XY (or LL / LR) on the same spot; splitting modes (NiPS3 P2, CoPS3 P2) are only separable this way.
66	- Resonance changes multiphonon intensities (Kim 2019) and Raman markers of T_N are laser-wavelength sensitive
67	  (Martin-Perez 2023, corpus p.2).
68	
69	## Pitfalls
70	- Laser heating: local heating can suppress order and shift the apparent T_N; low power and power series are needed
71	  (Martin-Perez 2023, corpus p.2; Sun 2019 used 0.17 mW).
72	- Label confusion (P2 at 117 vs 155 cm-1 in different MnPS3 papers).
73	- Absence of a splitting in 1L is not proof of no order (Kim 2021 domain argument).
74	
75	## What to ask
76	- Temperature series and its spacing around T_N; laser power and wavelength; polarization configuration.
77	- Layer number and substrate; strain; time in air; field direction if magnons are claimed.
78	
79	## Reference figures
80	- arXiv 1901.10890 (Kim 2019, NiPS3) Fig. 3: two-magnon versus T and thickness; Fig. 4: Delta P2 versus T; Fig. 5:
81	  T_N versus thickness.
82	- arXiv 2108.10945 (Vaclavkova 2021, FePS3) Fig. 1: T map 4.2 to 300 K and magneto-Raman magnon-phonon coupling.
83	- doi:10.1103/physrevb.103.235411 (Liu 2021, CoPS3) Figs. 3-4: P2 splitting and two-magnon (arXiv id not verified).

  doi:10.1103/physrevlett.127.097401, corpus p.2; 4L). In few layers it was seen only well below T_N (about 60 K)
  near 120 cm-1 (Ghosh 2021, corpus p.1).
- Field along c: M splits into branches; the lower branch anticrosses P1 to P3 (magnon-polarons), and an extra R1 mode
  appears at high field (Vaclavkova 2021, corpus p.3, Fig. 1b; Liu 2021, up to 30 T).
- Thickness: DISPUTED. Lee et al. 2016 (Nano Lett. 16, 7433, arXiv 1608.04169) report Ising order to 1L with little
  T_N change; Wang et al. 2016 (2D Mater. 3, 031009) report a T_N drop with thinning (both relayed by Martin-Perez
  et al. 2023, ACS Nano, doi:10.1021/acsnano.2c11654, corpus p.2). Magnetometry on 5 to 9 layer flakes gives T_N
  about 4 K below bulk (114.3 versus 118 K) (Martin-Perez 2023, corpus p.5). Strain alone can lower T_N (same, p.2).
- Air: 2L FePS3 Raman stable up to 6 days in ambient (Lee 2016, Suppl. Fig. S16, corpus p.38).

## MnPS3 (T_N about 78 K)
- Mode near 155 cm-1 involves Mn; it disappears near 80 K and a mode at 151 cm-1 appears below about 50 K (130L flake,
  488 nm, 0.17 mW to avoid heating) (Sun et al. 2019, J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 10, 3087, doi:10.1021/acs.jpclett.9b00758,
  corpus p.2, p.4-5). Sun et al. also infer transitions near 120, 80 and 55 K (corpus p.2).
- T_N from broadening, abrupt redshift and spectral-weight gain of the 155 cm-1 peak: about 78 K bulk, about 66 K 3L
  (Lim 2021, corpus p.2, p.11).
- Frequencies are nearly constant from 2L to bulk (weak interlayer coupling); 3L-4L show only P5, P6; 2L only P6; 1L
  gave no signal (degradation or weak scattering) (Sun 2019, corpus p.3-4).
- Below T_N (Oliva 2023, 3.4 K): a mode near 117 cm-1 vanishes and new peaks appear near 194, 370, 565, 605 cm-1, of
  unknown origin; the mode near 154 cm-1 is the most T-sensitive. Its two-magnon interpretation is ruled out
  (two-magnon expected near 177 cm-1); origin DISPUTED (Oliva 2023, corpus p.4, p.7-8).
- A spin-glass-like short-range regime below about 120 K is proposed from linewidths (Oliva 2023, corpus p.6).

## NiPS3 (bulk T_N 155 K)
- P2 (near 180 cm-1) splits into Ag (XX, higher) and Bg (XY, lower) below T_N; Delta P2 tracks the susceptibility and
  is near zero at 295 K (Kim 2019, corpus p.4-5, Fig. 4). Two-magnon continuum in XY grows and blueshifts on cooling;
  the Fano asymmetry |1/q| of a high-frequency phonon (P9) rises below T_N (Kim 2019, corpus p.3-5, Fig. 3).
- Thickness: order persists to 2L with slightly lower T_N; Kim 2019 conclude it is suppressed in 1L (same on hBN and
  SiO2). DISPUTED: Kim T. Y. et al. 2021 (Nano Lett. 21, 10114, doi:10.1021/acs.nanolett.1c03992, corpus p.2, p.5)
  argue 1L orders but the D3d monolayer's three zigzag domains make Delta P2 unmeasurable in XX/XY. Discala et al.
  2024 (Adv. Phys. Res. 3, 2300096) also question bulk-Hamiltonian assumptions (corpus p.1-2).
- Multiphonon peaks near 210, 590, 800 cm-1 are resonance dependent and not magnetic (Kim 2019, corpus p.4).

## CoPS3
- Monolayer about 0.80 nm. P2 near 149 cm-1 splits into P2' (Ag) and P2'' (Bg) at low T (XY vs XX); Delta P2 > 8 cm-1
  below about 56 K, near zero above about 100 K; bulk transition 118 K (Liu Q. et al. 2021, PRB 103, 235411,
  doi:10.1103/physrevb.103.235411, corpus p.3-4, Figs. 2-3). Splitting is layer independent (intralayer distortion).
- Two-magnon bands near 350 and 600 cm-1 in XY in 1L; Fano P8 below 56 K (Liu 2021, corpus p.4-5, Fig. 4). The
  authors interpret few-layer behaviour as BKT-like (T_KT about 100 K); interpretation, not consensus.

## Polarization, excitation, quality
- Use XX and XY (or LL / LR) on the same spot; splitting modes (NiPS3 P2, CoPS3 P2) are only separable this way.
- Resonance changes multiphonon intensities (Kim 2019) and Raman markers of T_N are laser-wavelength sensitive
  (Martin-Perez 2023, corpus p.2).

## Pitfalls
- Laser heating: local heating can suppress order and shift the apparent T_N; low power and power series are needed
  (Martin-Perez 2023, corpus p.2; Sun 2019 used 0.17 mW).
- Label confusion (P2 at 117 vs 155 cm-1 in different MnPS3 papers).
- Absence of a splitting in 1L is not proof of no order (Kim 2021 domain argument).

## What to ask
- Temperature series and its spacing around T_N; laser power and wavelength; polarization configuration.
- Layer number and substrate; strain; time in air; field direction if magnons are claimed.

## Reference figures
- arXiv 1901.10890 (Kim 2019, NiPS3) Fig. 3: two-magnon versus T and thickness; Fig. 4: Delta P2 versus T; Fig. 5:
  T_N versus thickness.
- arXiv 2108.10945 (Vaclavkova 2021, FePS3) Fig. 1: T map 4.2 to 300 K and magneto-Raman magnon-phonon coupling.
- doi:10.1103/physrevb.103.235411 (Liu 2021, CoPS3) Figs. 3-4: P2 splitting and two-magnon (arXiv id not verified).

# Artifacts and red flags in Raman spectra of 2D materials

Each entry: what it looks like, how to tell it from a real band, what to do. Sources in brackets.

## Cosmic-ray spikes
- One to three pixels wide, far narrower than any phonon line at the instrument resolution, present in one
  acquisition only. Real lines have the instrument's minimum width and repeat across accumulations or angles.
- Remove before fitting (modified z-score on the first difference: Whitaker and Hayes, Chemom. Intell. Lab. Syst.
  179, 82, 2018). In an angle series, replace spike pixels from the most similar frame (Barton and Hennelly, Appl.
  Spectrosc. 73, 893, 2019). List them under artifacts, never under peaks.

## Silicon substrate
- First-order Si line near 520.7 cm-1 (a widely used calibration convention; check the offset of the fitted
  position and flag a calibration problem when it exceeds about 1 cm-1; 520 to 520.9 is reported in practice, Lee
  et al. 2010 and Castellanos-Gomez et al. 2014). Second-order Si features near 950 and 980 cm-1 (Gillet et al.
  2017, arXiv 1708.05874, Fig. 1) and a 2TA band computed near 300 cm-1 (same paper, DFPT) can be mistaken for
  sample modes. Brillouin scattering from Si gives a line near
  4.5 cm-1 in ultra-low-frequency setups (Zhang et al., PRB 87, 115413, 2013).
- Assign these as 'Si substrate'. A strong Si line with weak sample bands suggests a thin flake.

## Calibration
- First-order wavelength calibration errors of 5 to 7 cm-1 have been reported (Lee et al., Nat. Commun. 3, 1024,
  2012). Shifts of 1 to 3 cm-1 (layer number, strain, doping) are only meaningful after a calibration check.

## Background
- Broad fluorescence or photoluminescence slopes; remove with an asymmetric least-squares baseline (arPLS or
  asPLS). For broad bands (disordered carbon D and G, amorphous phases) a global baseline can eat real signal: fit
  a local linear background together with the peaks. A Breit-Wigner-Fano line shape can absorb a background slope;
  compare line shapes by BIC.

## Low-wavenumber cutoff
- Notch and edge filters block the region near the laser line (Bragg notch filters reach about 5 to 10 cm-1,
  Zhang et al. 2013). A missing shear or breathing mode below the cutoff is not evidence of absence.

## Plasma lines
- Laser plasma lines have a fixed absolute wavelength, so their Raman shift changes when the laser changes; they
  are very narrow and do not belong to the sample. Suspect them when a narrow line has no assignment.

## Laser heating
- Phonon lines soften and broaden with temperature. Graphene G shifts about -0.016 cm-1/K (Calizo et al., Nano
  Lett. 7, 2645, 2007); 1L WS2 about -0.0093 (E) and -0.0122 (A1g) cm-1/K (Huang et al., Sci. Rep. 2016);
  few-layer MoS2 about -0.013 and -0.012 cm-1/K (Sahoo et al., arXiv 1302.5865). A power series is the test.

## Substrate interference
- On SiO2/Si, absolute intensities and intensity ratios depend on oxide thickness and laser wavelength: graphene
  I(2D)/I(G) changed by almost 370 % for a 60 % change in SiO2 thickness (Yoon et al., PRB 80, 125422, 2009).
  Never read layer number from absolute intensity or from I(2D)/I(G) without the substrate stack.

## Resonance
- Near an excitonic resonance, second-order bands can exceed first-order ones. WS2 at 514 to 532 nm: 2LA(M) lies
  about 4 cm-1 below E2g and overlaps it (Berkdemir et al., Sci. Rep. 3, 1755, 2013; Mitioglu et al., PRB 89,
  245442, 2014). Fit both or the E2g position and layer count are wrong.

## Saturation and clipping
- A flat-topped peak or values at the detector maximum: the peak shape and intensity are wrong; ask for a shorter
  exposure.

1	# Measurement and analysis pitfalls common to 2D-material Raman
2	
3	Numbers only where read in the cited source (locator in brackets). [practice] marks common laboratory
4	practice that I could not tie to a source read for this note; treat it as advice, not evidence. Material
5	specifics are in graphene.md, hBN.md, black-phosphorus.md; spectrum-level artifacts also in ../artifacts.md.

# Measurement and analysis pitfalls common to 2D-material Raman

Numbers only where read in the cited source (locator in brackets). [practice] marks common laboratory
practice that I could not tie to a source read for this note; treat it as advice, not evidence. Material
specifics are in graphene.md, hBN.md, black-phosphorus.md; spectrum-level artifacts also in ../artifacts.md.

## Calibration and spectral accuracy
- A first-order (linear) pixel-to-wavelength calibration of a single-grating spectrograph gave Raman shift
  errors of 5.0 to -6.8 cm-1 across the detector; with only 3 Hg lines, up to 18 cm-1; adding the quadratic
  term brought it within +-0.3 cm-1 (Lee et al. 2012, Nat. Commun. 3, 1024; arXiv 1209.0234, Methods p.10).
  Their check: graphite G 1581.5 +- 0.3 cm-1 over 12 spots.
- The error depends on where on the detector a line falls, so a single Si-line check near 520 cm-1 does not
  validate a 2D band near 2700 cm-1 [inference from the same mechanism].
- Si first order is quoted as 520 (Lee et al. 2010, ACS Nano 4, 2695; arXiv 1005.2509) and 520.9 cm-1
  (Castellanos-Gomez et al. 2014, arXiv 1403.0499, p.7) in different setups: small offsets between labs are
  normal, so compare shifts relative to an internal reference measured in the same session.

## Resolution, grating and instrument line shape
- Measure resolution from the Rayleigh line: 1.9 vs 9.4 cm-1 on two instruments in one study; spectra then fit
  with Voigt profiles and the Lorentzian FWHM taken as the lifetime width (Das et al. 2008, Nat. Nanotechnol.
  3, 210; arXiv 0709.1174, p.2). About 0.6 cm-1 with a triple-filter low-frequency setup (Zhang et al. 2013,
  PRB 87, 115413; arXiv 1212.6796, p.2); 2.7 cm-1 in Lee 2010 (docs/verified-reference-numbers.md).
- Widths near the resolution (hBN 3 to 9 cm-1, BP Ag2 3 to 7 cm-1; see material notes) are instrument-limited:
  never compare raw FWHM across setups without the resolution. A 0.5 cm-1 resolution was not enough to count BP
  layers from positions (Castellanos-Gomez 2014, p.8).

## Laser heating, power density and photodamage
- Do a power series: Ferrari et al. 2006 saw no change from about 4 to 0.04 mW at 100x (arXiv
  cond-mat/0606284, p.2); typical working powers 1 mW with about 1 um spot (Cancado et al. 2011, arXiv
  1105.0175, p.2), 0.23 mW (Zhang 2013, p.2), below 300 uW at 0.5 NA (Janzen et al. 2023, arXiv 2306.13358,
  p.7). Quote power density, not power: the same mW gives different heating at different NA.
- Temperature coefficients depend on support: graphene 2D -0.034 cm-1/K supported vs -0.072 suspended
  (Calizo 2007, arXiv 0708.1223, Table I; Chen et al. via Lee et al. 2011, arXiv 1103.3337, p.2). Do not
  convert a shift into a temperature with a coefficient from a different geometry.
- Optothermal estimates need a peak-vs-T calibration, the absorbed (not incident) power, and a measured spot
  size; using two spot sizes helps (Malekpour and Balandin 2018, J. Raman Spectrosc. 49, 106; arXiv
  1710.09749, pp.4, 18).
- Stokes/anti-Stokes thermometry fails under resonance when incident and scattered windows differ (Ferrari
  and Basko 2013, Nat. Nanotechnol. 8, 235; arXiv 1306.5856, p.12).
- Photodamage is dose-dependent: BP oxidation rate scales with fluence (Favron et al. 2015, arXiv 1408.0345,
  p.7); MnPS3 degraded at about 50 uW when one spot was illuminated 500 s or longer (Lim et al. 2021, Curr.
  Appl. Phys. 21, 1; doi 10.1016/j.cap.2020.09.017, pp.6-7, via Lit-RAG). Irreversible change in a repeat
  spectrum means damage, reversible shift means heating.

## Objective NA, focus and polarization
- A tightly focused beam has longitudinal (out-of-plane) field components that can excite modes forbidden for
  purely in-plane fields (Grosche et al. 2020, Opt. Express, doi 10.1364/OE.388943; arXiv 1905.12325,
  abstract). How large this leakage is for a standard 100x/0.9 objective was not quantified in what I read.
  [magnitude not verified]
- In birefringent crystals the classical Raman tensor fails because polarization changes with depth; an
  effective tensor is needed (Kranert et al. 2016, PRL 116, 127401, abstract). In thin anisotropic flakes on
  SiO2/Si, anisotropic interference changes polar patterns with thickness (Kim et al. 2015, arXiv 1510.03263).
- Si substrate intensity depends on Si crystal orientation to the laser polarization (Castellanos-Gomez 2014,
  p.8): sample/Si intensity ratios need fixed sample rotation.
- Ask whether the analyzer is fixed and a half-wave plate rotates the polarization, or the sample rotates;
  grating efficiency is polarization dependent [practice].

## Interference on SiO2/Si
- Graphene I(2D)/I(G) changed by almost 370 % for a 60 % change in SiO2 thickness (Yoon et al. 2009, PRB 80,
  125422; arXiv 0908.4322, abstract, Fig. 2). Intensity ratios between bands at different shifts are
  stack-dependent.
- For MoS2 the sample intensity oscillates with thickness (interference maxima), but the ratio of sample to Si
  intensity becomes monotonic and gives thickness (Li et al. 2012, ACS Nano 6, 7381; arXiv 1308.3835,
  abstract, Fig. 4). Interference also changes optical contrast (Gorbachev et al. 2011, arXiv 1008.2868).

## Encapsulation and overlayers
- hBN encapsulation narrows graphene 2D (16 to 20 vs above 22 cm-1 on SiO2) and changes doping (Neumann et
  al. 2015, arXiv 1406.7771, p.2); it narrows BP lines and reveals a surface mode (Urban et al., arXiv
  1711.08294, abstract). Compare encapsulated with encapsulated only.
- Overlayer lines can overlap sample lines: hBN E2g near 1366 cm-1 on graphene D (Purdie et al. 2018, Nat.
  Commun. 9, 5387, p.6, via Lit-RAG). Measure an overlayer-only reference spot.

## Low-frequency modes and filters
- Shear and breathing modes (tens of cm-1) need notch or Bragg filters reaching about 5 to 10 cm-1 and
  plasma-line cleanup (Zhang 2013, p.2). Many production spectrometers cut above the graphene C mode, so absence
  below the cutoff is not evidence (Ferrari and Basko 2013, p.2). Odd and even layer numbers scale differently
  (Zhang 2013, abstract).

## Spikes, plasma lines, fluorescence, baseline
- Spikes and plasma lines: see ../artifacts.md (sources listed there, not re-verified here).
- Fluorescence or PL backgrounds: fit a local background with the peaks for broad bands; a global baseline can
  remove real broad signal [practice; see ../artifacts.md].

## Fitting line shapes and over-fitting
- Report whether ratios use heights or areas: graphene defect relations use heights (Cancado 2011) and heights
  and areas diverge in stage 2 (Eckmann et al. 2012, arXiv 1207.2058, p.5).
- Number of components needs physics: 1L graphene 2D one, Bernal 2L four (Ferrari 2006, p.2); unresolved
  doublets (BP Ag2 in few layers, resolved only at 77 K, Favron 2015, p.10) appear as broadening. Adding peaks
  without a physical reason fits noise; compare models by an information criterion [practice].
- Fit overlapping neighbours jointly (WS2 2LA(M) and E2g, see ../artifacts.md; hBN and graphene D, Purdie 2018).

## Comparing spectra from different setups
- Different lasers: dispersive bands (graphene D, 2D) move; resonances change relative intensities (Cancado
  2011; Kim et al. 2012, arXiv 1201.4221). Different spectrographs: calibration offsets of several cm-1 (Lee
  2012). Different substrates: interference changes ratios (Yoon 2009). Compare differences measured in one
  session, not absolute values across papers.

## Mapping statistics
- A spectrum averages over the spot: sub-spot strain variations show up as width, not shift (Neumann 2015,
  Fig. 1); mono- and bilayers can vary strongly from sample to sample (Gorbachev 2011, p.4).
- Use many points and correlations: hundreds of map pixels per sample fell on a G-2D line of slope 2.2 (Lee
  2012, p.3, Fig. 2). Report distributions (histograms, median and spread), not one "representative" spectrum.
- Move the spot between acquisitions on sensitive materials (Lim 2021).

## What to ask
- Laser line and power at sample, objective NA, spot size; grating, resolution, calibration lines and date.
- Substrate stack and oxide thickness; encapsulation; suspended or supported.
- Polarization geometry; temperature and atmosphere; exposure time; number of spectra and map size.

## Reference figures
- Yoon 2009, arXiv 0908.4322, Fig. 2: G and 2D intensities and their ratio vs SiO2 thickness.
- Li 2012, arXiv 1308.3835, Fig. 4: MoS2/Si intensity ratios vs layer number, calculated and measured.
- Zhang 2013, arXiv 1212.6796, Fig. 4: shear and breathing positions vs layer number (odd vs even).
- Neumann 2015, arXiv 1406.7771, Fig. 1: maps and 2D-width histograms, hBN vs SiO2 support.

The matcher's top hit (CdPS3, DFT, score 0.60) is a different compound and shows only that the pattern is MPS3-like.

Literature positions were read from a figure (arXiv 1608.04169 Fig. 1b, 300 K), with about ±3 cm-1 reading error. The 7 to 15 cm-1 offset is larger than that error, but I did not verify the numbers in the text tables. A second FePS3 reference (for example Vaclavkova et al. 2021, arXiv 2108.10945, Fig. 1) was not compared.

Calibration: one Si line at 520.87 cm-1 (offset +0.17) validates the calibration only near 520 cm-1. Literature reports detector-position-dependent calibration errors that a single Si line cannot exclude (general-measurement.md, Calibration). Discriminating tests: a power series at 295 K, a Si-referenced repeat on another flake, and a comparison spectrum of a verified FePS3 flake on the same stack.
The 550.7 cm-1 band lies outside the range of the FePS3 figure used (50 to 450 cm-1), so its FePS3 assignment is inferred from the MPS3 note only.
The 74.7 cm-1 peak sits near the low-wavenumber cutoff of the window (60.5 cm-1) and is not assigned; it may be a filter-edge or background artifact, not a phonon.
Irreps are not assigned: the matcher's Ag/Bg labels belong to the CdPS3 DFT entry, and no polarization series was measured (single spectrum). Layer number and defect level are not determined.
Laser power, spot size, and resolution are not given in the metadata, so the instrument-limited FWHM cannot be separated from intrinsic linewidth.

It matches 123.7, 240.6, 263.5, 368.7 and 550.7 cm-1 to DFT modes within 0.6 cm-1 and has no missing strong modes. This is a DFT entry for a different metal thiophosphate, so it shows the mode pattern is MPS3-like, not the identity of the cation.

The stated material. The qualitative pattern matches the bulk FePS3 room-temperature spectrum in arXiv 1608.04169 Fig. 1b (weak broad low-frequency P1 near 100 cm-1, weak P3 near 230, P4 near 248, P5 near 278, strongest P6 near 380 cm-1), and the MPS3 note says the paramagnetic phase above T_N=118 K has a broad low-frequency band plus four modes in 150 to 400 cm-1. However, the sample's sharp modes sit 7 to 15 cm-1 below those values (P4 240.6 vs about 248, P5 263.5 vs about 278, P6 368.7 vs about 380). The Si line is calibrated to 520.87 (offset +0.17), so calibration does not explain the difference. No FePS3 entry exists in the local DFT or literature tables, so this cannot be confirmed quantitatively.
